events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: A Hero Rises

options.text: Rally the common people to take up arms and prepare to fight!
Call in a favor from a rural tribe of fierce warriors, who have pledged to aid you.
Our elite elephant corps will trample and terrorize the enemy!

events.text: The [rival] are angry and they are coming for blood. War has been declared. However, you are a hero to the people of [rival]. With one word they will rally to the defense of the nation.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: A Plot Took Shape

options.text: Whatever [character] and [character] are planning, it cannot go unchallenged.
Whatever [character] and [character] are planning, there is little to be done.

events.text: You had not supposed [character] would be so willing to interfere in [rival] politics. And yet, [rival] agents gained access to the prison in [city], freeing [character] and a number of other dissidents and secreting them across the border.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: A Twisted Scheme

options.text: We shall gamble on peace.
Embrace the certainty of war!
This is merely a ruse to train his army, easily dealt with.

events.text: [character] of [rival] is preparing for war against us. [character], being a Schemer Archetype, was bound to betray us sooner or later, but perhaps it might be possible to delay his attack by paying tribute. However, this may simply allow the [rival] to further build up their forces to launch a more powerful attack in the future.

events.text: [character] of [rival] is preparing for war against us. Beware, this may simply allow the [rival] to further build up their forces to launch a more powerful attack in the future.

While this may simply allow the [rival] to further build up their forces to launch a more powerful attack in the future, his nature may well cause him to plot against another empire in the meantime.

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: A War Demand

options.text: Very well, we will send money...
We will assist with your research...
Never!

events.text: An emissary from [rival] arrives by horseback, escorted by a team of the finest [rival] soldiers. He carries a message. [character] is willing to avoid conflict, but only if we pay tribute.

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Agitated Nation

options.text: Agree to tribute to delay an armed conflict.
Recruit the finest ranged units in [rival].
Prepare for war by training infantry units.

events.text: The [rival] have grown displeased with us, and we stand on the brink of war. A twitchy messenger insists that conflict may still be avoided... if we agree to a tribute. Shall we believe him?

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Agitated Nation

options.text: Pay tribute to the [rival].
Deploy new mounted units to the front.
Recruit the finest ranged units in [rival].

events.text: [rival] is preparing to attack, but their emissary says that [rival] units will stand down if we pay tribute. What shall we tell him?

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Agitated Nation

options.text: We prefer tribute over bloodshed.
Our armies will wipe them from the battlefield.
Our elephants will trample them into the dirt.

events.text: We knew this day was coming. [rival] has sent a sneering emissary to court, requesting that we pay them tribute. With our gold.... or our lives. What is our reply?

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Agitated Nation

options.text: Pay tribute to appease the [rival].
Let us instruct you in the arts of war.
Our resources may well be limited. Our will to fight is not.

events.text: The leadership of [rival] desires war. A visiting emissary comes before the court, demanding that we pay tribute or face their martial wrath. How shall we respond?

options.text: They won't dare attack us in the near term if we strengthen our military.

events.text: Our operatives tell us that the [rival] are upset enough with us to consider hostilities. Only a skilled diplomat could reverse this trend.

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Anger Erupts

options.text: Commission new infantry units and rally the nation to defend against this threat.
Deploy new ranged troops and pore over maps to determine where to strike.
Our cavalry will outmaneuver the enemy and take the battle to them.
An inspiring speech should be enough for our veteran troops.

events.text: The [rival], who have been angry with us for some time, have sent an emissary with a declaration of war.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Antihero

options.text: Oh mighty [character], please spare us your wrath!
We shall meet the [rival] on the battlefield!
It is [character] who shall be crushed, by my hand!

events.text: Word has reached us that the [rival] are planning to attack us. Their ruler, the great Hero Archetype [character] has vowed to crush our armies and tear down our cities with his bare hands. Yet it might still be possible to avert this war by paying tribute and placating his ego.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Antihero

options.text: Oh mighty [character], please spare us your wrath!
We shall meet the [rival] on the battlefield!

events.text: Word has reached us that the [rival] are furious with us and are planning to invade. Their ruler, the great Hero Archetype [character] has vowed to crush us, to drive our people before him, and hear the lamentations of our women. Yet it might still be possible to avert this war by paying a large tribute and placating his ego.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Antihero

options.text: Oh mighty [character], please spare us your wrath!
We shall meet the [rival] on the battlefield!
It is [character] who shall be crushed, by my hand!

events.text: Word has reached us that the [rival] are considering attacking us. Their ruler, the great Hero Archetype [character] has vowed to crush our armies and tear down our cities with his bare hands should this come to pass. Yet it should be possible to avert this war by paying tribute and placating his ego.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Assassination of Monarch

options.text: We accept. Prepare a feast for their men.
Stall them while we consider other options.

events.text: The [rival] have assassinated our ruler! Now they demand that the widower, [character], marries their ruler. They have sent 20 of their finest men as an armed escort. Otherwise, they will invade us and kill the new child king! What is our command?

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Betrothed to War

options.text: I will not go to war with [rival] on behalf of your homeland, [character].
We will ride to the aid of [rival], dearest [character]!
I weep for the plight of [rival], but we cannot wage war on behalf of another Nation.

events.text: Your husband [character] looks on in helpless desperation at the war between his homeland of [rival] and the [rival]. He demands that you come to the aid of his people in this time of crisis. [character] reminds you that the proud [rival] have certain expectations of a monarch who has married into one of their leading Family; they will tolerate no neutrality on your part in their conflicts. As such, should we refuse to join their cause, the [rival] will consider us to be their enemy as well. Will you join the [rival] war against the [rival] on behalf of your spouse [character]?

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Breaking the Covenant

options.text: We are in no position to upset the [rival]. Break off the alliance with [rival].
Curse these ignoble [rival]. We won't betray our [rival] allies.

events.text: The [rival] must truly hold us in contempt. They have dared to demand that we break off our alliance with [rival]. If we refuse, there will be war! Can our honor be so cheaply bought?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Calling for War

options.text: [rival] will pay for their crimes.
They are not our rivals.

events.text: It is rare to see the families unite, but here they stand. [character], [character] and [character] are all gathered before the throne, together calling for war against [rival]. This rival power has been vying for your lands for too long, and the families think it time to turn the tides. Will [rival] march to war?

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Choosing Sides

options.text: We despise such ultimatums. [rival] has done us no harm. See you on the battlefield!
I see that [character] gives us no choice in the matter. We will join you [rival] in open warfare against [rival]!

events.text: Envoys from the bellicose [rival] have arrived, demanding that we join them in their ongoing war with [rival]. The [rival] will tolerate no neutrality in this dispute. Should we refuse to choose sides in the conflict, they will consider us complicit in the real or imagined schemes of [rival], and in turn declare war on us.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Collision Course

tip: As leader: +10% Height From Modifier / Hill
As general: +25% Height From Modifier / Hill

options.text: We shall find a way...
... or make one!

events.text: In a brash move, the [rival] have seized a key mountain pass, threatening our expansion. Their ruler, [character], waits for our reaction, armies at the ready. Is this a time for caution, or will we call his bluff?

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Commander Crisis

options.text: Take this gold and campaign elsewhere!
Bring your armies, take home your dead.
Forewarned is forearmed.

events.text: The famous Commander Archetype, [character] is rumored to be planning a campaign against us! At the head of the [rival] armies, he will be a formidable foe. Our one chance to avoid war is to pre-empt it with an offer of tribute.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Commander Crisis

options.text: Take this gold and campaign elsewhere!
Bring your armies, take home your dead.

events.text: The famous Commander Archetype, [character] is furiously planning a campaign against us! At the head of the [rival] armies, he will be a formidable foe. Our one chance to avoid war is to pre-empt it with a generous offer of tribute.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Commander Crisis

options.text: Take this gold and campaign elsewhere!
Bring your armies, take home your dead.
Forewarned is forearmed.

events.text: The famous Commander Archetype, [character] is rumored to be thinking of a campaign against us! At the head of the [rival] armies, he could be a formidable foe. Our one chance to avoid war is to pre-empt it with an offer of tribute.

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Crimes in [rival]

options.text: Offer to judge these cases, personally. Trials will begin within the month.
As upset as they are, the best course is to permit them to apply their own laws to these cases.
Refuse to allow our citizens to be subject to foreign laws.

events.text: [rival], who is already upset with us, has sent an emissary to deliver a list of grievances. They accuse some of our citizens of criminal incidents and demand that we provide justice.

events.author: Soren Johnson / Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Demand For Knowledge

options.text: I suppose we haven't much choice in the matter...
[rival] will not be bullied.

events.text: An envoy from [rival] arrived at court today and demanded an audience. The delegate wastes no time on pleasantries. "[character] demands that you share with us what you know of [tech] or face dire consequences."

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Diplomacy By Other Means

options.text: Perhaps gold can buy peace?
Attack now before he can find allies!
Come now, it’s always worth talking!

events.text: The renowned Diplomat Archetype [character] of [rival] no longer believes that we are worth talking to. Instead, he intends to form a coalition of other nations to “end our menace once and for all.” This is obviously less than ideal.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Diplomacy By Other Means

options.text: Perhaps gold can buy peace?
Attack now before he can find allies!

events.text: The renowned Diplomat Archetype [character] of [rival], driven by his great anger, no longer believes that we are worth talking to. Instead, he intends to form a coalition of other nations to “end our menace once and for all.” This is obviously less than ideal.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Diplomacy By Other Means

options.text: Perhaps gold can buy peace?
Attack now before he can find allies!
Come now, it’s always worth talking!

events.text: The renowned Diplomat Archetype [character] of [rival] is losing faith that we are worth talking to. Instead, he contemplates the need to form a coalition of other nations to force us to make concessions. This is obviously less than ideal.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Disrespect

options.text: Stains are easier to remove than invading armies.
Would you care to draft the court's response then, [character]?

events.text: From the look on [character] face, you would think the [rival] were demanding firstborn children, rather than iron shipments. "Does [character] really think [rival] is so weak as to grovel at his passing whim? Any response but to spit in his face would be too kind and a stain on [rival] honor."

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Distant Nation Threatens

options.text: Agree to whatever they demand.
They are too far away to be a threat.

events.text: Emissaries arrive from the distant nation of [rival]. They ignore court protocol and give a spiteful speech. "Your nation shall pay tribute to [character], or we shall move against you in force." What shall we do?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Enslaved by Egypt

options.text: We cannot interfere with [rival]'s affairs.
Demand that [rival] allow its slaves to purchase their freedom.
This is the perfect excuse to attack [rival]!

events.text: [religion] leaders have come to appeal for royal assistance. They claim that many of their people are enslaved by the nation of [rival], and they wish for us to intervene. Dabbling in foreign affairs is a tricky thing, and we should make decisions wisely.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Gifts by Swordpoint

options.text: Our generosity is as famous as our [resource].
They can pry the [resource] from our dead hands.

events.text: [rival] merchants, escorted by armed soldiers, arrive in the capital to negotiate a new trade deal. The deal? [rival] requires a generous gift of [resource], or they will send their armies to take it by force.

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Grievances

options.text: Offer to adjudicate over these cases, personally. Hold trials within the year.
Let us forge a treaty of extradition, so criminals will face justice agreeable to both peoples.
We will look into these matters for you. This may take some time to complete.

events.text: An emissary from [rival] brings a list of grievances before us. Some of your citizens are accused of crimes against their people and interests. The emissary demands justice in these cases.

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: Holy War

options.text: We have no quarrel with the [rival], heathens or not.
The pious [character] is right. These blasphemous [rival] must be silenced!
Regardless of their many heresies, there is no need for war with the [rival].

events.text: The Righteous [character] demands we join his holy war against the heathen [rival] in the name of [religion]! The zealous [rival] will tolerate no neutrality in this conflict. Should we refuse to join their cause, they will consider us complicit in the heresies of [rival], and in turn declare war on us. The [religion] establishment would also see our refusal as a sign of insufficient piety. Shall we join the [rival] holy war for [religion] against the pagan [rival]?

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Holy War

options.text: May your Gods accept this gift to spare us!
Only [rival] Gods can judge us!
[rival] Gods shall smite these unbelievers!

events.text: The Zealot Archetype [character] has begun to preach against us. He claims that the [rival] Gods have cast judgement upon us and it is his holy duty to destroy us! This crusade against us will likely soon begin in earnest, unless we can placate them with tribute.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Holy War

options.text: May your Gods accept this gift to spare us!
Only [rival] Gods can judge us!

events.text: The Zealot Archetype [character], enraged, has begun preaching against us. He claims that the [rival] Gods have cast judgement upon us and it is his holy duty to destroy us! This crusade against us will likely soon begin in earnest, unless we can placate them with huge tribute.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Holy War

options.text: May your Gods accept this gift to bless us!
Only [rival] Gods can judge us!
[rival] Gods shall smite these unbelievers!

events.text: The Zealot Archetype [character] has chastised us during one of his sermons. He claims that the [rival] Gods are displeased with us and it is his holy duty to warn us to repent!

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Honorable Mention

options.text: Thank [character] for his honorable efforts.
Warn the [rival] King that he better find a way to dissuade them next time, for his own sake.
I’m afraid our best chance against [rival] is a preemptive strike. Call in the guards.

events.text: On a diplomatic mission to the capital, [character] requests a private audience. His stern expression suggests a serious matter on his mind. “[title] [character], I must warn you that some in [rival] wish to wage war with [rival]. I do not suffer the same affliction of short memory and recall clearly that [rival] provided us with much needed Food during the Drought. I have dissuaded their efforts to wage war for the time being, but I doubt I will be able to do so again when the topic next arises.”

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Immortal Peril

options.text: Yes, my soul believes this is the right choice.
No, I will not discuss matters of faith.

events.text: A procession of zealots from [rival] visit the court, preaching the tenets of [religion]. It is more than a display. They carry with them an ultimatum: refuse [religion] at your immortal peril.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Insolent Generals

tip: As leader: +50 Unit Trait XP / Infantry
As governor: +100 Unit Trait XP / Infantry

options.text: Our people need thicker skin.
[rival] have always been cruel.

events.text: Visiting [rival] generals refer to our nation as "The Effeminate," and they mock our culture and our traditions. This behavior has become quite demoralizing to members of the court, and our people are beginning to gossip. What shall we do?

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Judgment Day

options.text: We shall make reparations.
We have nothing but contempt for his court!
Judge not, lest ye be judged!

events.text: [character], Judge Archetype of [rival], has turned his unerring judgment upon us. He believes he has taken our measure and found us wanting, and now he prepares to enforce his sentence through force of arms. If we wish to avoid war, we will have to pay a hefty fine.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Judgment Day

options.text: We shall make reparations.
We have nothing but contempt for his court!

events.text: [character], Judge Archetype of [rival], has turned his unerring judgment upon us, spurred on by his obvious rage. He believes he has taken our measure and found us wanting, and now he prepares to enforce his sentence through force of arms. If we wish to avoid war, we will have to pay a very hefty fine.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Judgment Day

options.text: We shall make reparations.
We have nothing but contempt for his court!
Judge not, lest ye be judged!

events.text: [character], Judge Archetype of [rival], has turned his unerring judgment upon us. He believes he has reason to investigate us, and if necessary he will prepare to enforce his sentence through force of arms. If we wish to avoid war, we will have to pay a mild fine.

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Making Amends

options.text: Let us reach out to them and offer to make good on one of their complaints.
We can tie them up in legal and diplomatic knots for a number of years.
Allowing them to declare war fits right in with our plans.

events.text: The [rival] stand ready to attack us. They have been angry with us for several reasons, some more legitimate than others. Not much time remains before a war is sure to begin.

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Moment of Weakness

options.text: [rival] was next, regardless. Do your worst.
Perhaps I can fool [rival] into confronting [rival] instead.

events.text: While your forces wage war against the soldiers of [rival], the court holds an audience with diplomats from [rival], who seem unusually confident. Sneering, they demand that we meet their terms, lest their own troops take advantage of our current vulnerability. We find ourselves between two armies. What is your command?

events.author: Gabe Campbell
events.name: No Neutral Option

options.text: Tell these [rival] envoys that we will meet their kinsmen on the battlefield.
Joining [character] in his war with the [rival] is agreeable to me.

events.text: The ongoing war between [rival] and [rival] leaves no room for neutrality. Freshly arrived [rival] envoys have made it clear that all nations are either with them or against them. This aggressive diplomacy is quite unconventional. However, there may be opportunities for us in a war with an enemy occupied on two fronts. How shall we answer this ultimatum?

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Our Peace is Over

options.text: Apologize for failing to please them.
[rival] does not grovel.

events.text: [rival] is no longer happy with us and has decided to end our Peace. How shall we respond?

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Raised Fist

options.text: [rival] will not stand for this.
We will pay what [character] asks.
Perhaps the leaders of our faith can find another solution.

events.text: A heavily guarded delegation arrives outside the capital. The [rival] refuse to enter the city and wait for us to come to them. As we near the solemn group, their leader raises a hand, motioning for us to come no closer. After a short silence, a stern voice carries across the field. “You stand accused of having brought the [event] to [rival]. [character] demands compensation, lest the might of [rival] fall upon you and smite this sickness from the land.”

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Rally the Nation

options.text: Deploy our special forces. We will take them by surprise!
Beef up our mounted unit contingent. Mobility wins wars.
We will strike the enemy from range and devastate their forces.
Boost our infantry and our defenses. Prepare to repel invaders.
Rally our veterans. Give them a reason to fight!

events.text: Emissaries arrive from [rival] bringing a declaration of war. The [rival] have been angry with us, so this is not much of a surprise. Now is the time to rally our nation to its defense.

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Repairing Ties

options.text: Send an emissary with an offer for us to make annual Tribute payments.
Gather more raw materials to construct new facilities and train new units.

events.text: Multiple sources indicate that the [rival] may be preparing to attack us, despite your amicable relations. Your court suggests that perhaps there is still an opportunity to keep the peace.

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Return Our Hostage

options.text: We will agree to these terms.
These terms are not acceptable.

events.text: Messengers reach the palace with an urgent proclamation from the court of [rival]. The [rival] are prepared to declare war unless we release our hostage. Only his speedy return will prevent a coming conflict. How shall we respond?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Save my Family

options.text: Assure [character] that we will ally with his people.
We must attempt to broker a truce.
This is not our fight.

events.text: [character] comes before the court to request support for his kin, the [tribe]. The Tribe is currently engaged in a battle for their survival against the powerful [rival] army. Is it wise to place ourselves in the middle of a foreign dispute?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Secret Strike

options.text: There is no honor in such machinations.
I should have thought of this plan myself.

events.text: Our top spies assemble a small group of military officials to share a piece of sensitive information. [character], ruler of [rival], is planning a diplomatic mission to [rival] when the seasons change. He will be traveling with fewer guards than usual. It is advised that we strike [character] down when he is vulnerable and frame the [rival] for his murder. This would pit our enemies against each other.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Secret Strike

options.text: I should have thought of this plan myself.
Offer troops to help escort [character].

events.text: Our top spies assemble a small group of military officials to share a piece of sensitive information. [character], ruler of [rival], is planning a diplomatic mission to [rival] when the seasons change. He will be traveling with fewer guards than usual. It is advised that we strike [character] down when he is vulnerable and frame the [rival] for his murder. This would pit our enemies against each other.

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Still Time

options.text: Send a warning to the leader of [rival], declaring our displeasure with the rumors.
Secure additional stone for fortifications, and train new archers to man them.

events.text: Rumors are circulating around the streets of [city] about a [rival] plan to declare war against our nation. Our advisors are urging us to take some form of action to calm the people.

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Submission

options.text: [rival] would rather fight than face dishonor.
Let us charm your men and forget these thoughts of war.

events.text: Armed soldiers of the [rival] military march through the streets of our capital at attention. Their leader, a pompous officer, preens before the court, offering an ominous threat. We must submit to [rival] or provide them with the requested tribute.

events.text: The shadow of the mighty [rival] army has loomed over our heads for years, and now it descends on [rival] at last. War ambassadors from [rival] have come with an ultimatum: we must agree to their terms or face the consequences.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Tactical Terror

options.text: Give peace a chance!
Strategy is the answer!
His tactics are predictable and can be countered.

events.text: [character], a cunning Tactician Archetype, is said to be planning an attack upon us. This could be disastrous as he is said to be unmatched on the battlefield. Perhaps if we offer tribute the [rival] can be placated for now.

Strategy is the answer!

events.text: [character], a cunning Tactician Archetype, is known to be besides himself with rage at us and plans to attack soon. This could be disastrous as he is said to be unmatched on the battlefield. Perhaps if we offer vast tribute the [rival] can be placated for now.

His tactics are predictable and can be countered.

events.text: [character], a cunning Tactician Archetype, may be planning an attack upon us. This would be disastrous, as he is said to be unmatched on the battlefield. Perhaps if we offer tribute the [rival] can be placated and friendly relations restored.

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Talk of War

options.text: Let us reach out to them with a gift.
Propose a research agreement.
Initiate a scholarly inquiry in search of an advantage we might obtain.

events.text: One of your informants from the [rival] court has sent a warning that there is increasing talk of the possibility of a looming war with us. This warning may give us an opening to make a move of our own to avoid such a conflict.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: The Final Campaign

options.text: The people will remember me in glory.
Now is not the time to wage new wars.
I wish to mend my relationship with [character].

events.text: You have built a legacy of victory that will long outlive your reign, but one more valiant campaign could further ensure your immortality. Tensions with [rival] have been escalating, and a single act of aggression may trigger their hostility. Sometimes, glory comes with a price.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Lure of Knowledge

options.text: Summon the troops. To war!
This is not our fight.
Lie and promise your aid to get your hands on the technology.

events.text: Stories of the war between [rival] and [rival] filter through to your court, leading to heated debates and nervous discussions as courtiers and advisers speculate on how the outcome of the war will affect [rival]. Such tales sound distant, but will [rival] neutrality last? A message arrives from [rival]: [character] asks you to join the fighting, offering a gift of technology if you agree to declare war on [rival]. How will we reply?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Ram with Two Horns

options.text: Vow to strike down the god's enemies yourself.
Commit your bow to fight Amani's enemies.
Refuse. [character] wields no power here.

events.text: The cult of Amani has unprecedented power within [rival], rumors claiming that in the distant past the priests could even command the King to take his own life. [character] may not wield that same power, but the religion is certainly still influential, wielding immense control over many in the court. Backed by these supporters, the [title] of Amani says that there are clear signs from the god that the time is right for war with [rival]. Shall the armies be gathered for war?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Scroll and the Spear

options.text: Send them our findings.
Then it is war.

events.text: The message from [rival] is terse, though the few lines leave a shadow over the court of [rival]. "We can not abide secrets. You will share your technology with us, or we will come and take it by force." What is our reply?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: The Stolen Scrolls

options.text: Such treachery must be met with war.
Tell [character] that he need only ask next time.
Demand repayment for their theft.

events.text: Your nation's teachers have reported a great theft of scrolls and tablets containing all manner of national secrets. The investigation initially seems fruitless until a farmer is found who saw a group of men fleeing in the night in a cart laden with documents. From their clothing and the path they took, it seems that [rival] are to blame.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: This Shall Not Stand

options.text: This matter cannot be worth the blood of thousands.
I would like to see them try.

events.text: It seems [rival] has, finally, decided that the imprisonment of [character] can no longer be tolerated. The forces of [rival] gather, and an ultimatum is issued: return the rightful king, or [rival] armies will.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Unlawful

options.text: We will fight because the cause is just.
Your grievances do not justify bloodshed.

events.text: After days of tense, private discussion, members of the [family] family emerge with a decree. They wish for us to wage a righteous war on [rival]. “[character] has built a flawed system, one which relies on the horrendous practice of [law]. It is time to tear down this abominable construct and erect something better in its place!”

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Unlawful

options.text: We will fight because the cause is just.
Your grievances do not justify bloodshed.

events.text: After days of tense, private discussion, members of the [family] family emerge with a decree. They wish for us to wage a righteous war on [rival]. “The famed Commander [character] has failed to give the most important order of all, to abolish the rite of [law] in [rival]. If he will not give the word, then we must do so in his place!”

They wish for us to wage a righteous war on [rival]. “[character] is said to be a great diplomat, but how can our empire sign any treaty with a realm beset by [law]? Only when this law has been fully repealed can our relations be normalized, and if [character] won’t do it then we must!”

options.text: We will fight because the cause is just.

events.text: After days of tense, private discussion, members of the [family] family emerge with a decree. They wish for us to wage a righteous war on [rival]. “His people think [character] a hero, yet what is heroic about allowing [law] in [rival]? The time has come to cast down [character] and free his people from such injustice!”

events.author: David Ballantyne

options.text: We will fight because the cause is just.

events.text: After days of tense, private discussion, members of the [family] family emerge with a decree. They wish for us to wage a righteous war on [rival]. “The ‘wise’ judge [character] has ruled in error by not striking down the unjust law of [law] in [rival]. We must rectify this injustice on the battlefield!”

events.author: David Ballantyne

options.text: We will fight because the cause is just.
Your grievances do not justify bloodshed.

events.text: After days of tense, private discussion, members of the [family] family emerge with a decree. They wish for us to wage a righteous war on [rival]. “The Orator, [character], speaks with a silver tongue, but no gilden words can cover the abominable [rival] practice of [law]. Where words fail, weapons can make a persuasive argument.”

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Unlawful

options.text: We will fight because the cause is just.
Your grievances do not justify bloodshed.

events.text: After days of tense, private discussion, members of the [family] family emerge with a decree. They wish for us to wage a righteous war on [rival]. “Who can understand the twisted machinations of a Schemer like [character]? But it is clear that he allows the accursed ordinance of [law] to continue in [rival]. The time has come to act directly. [law] must end!”

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Unlawful

options.text: We will fight because the cause is just.
Your grievances do not justify bloodshed.

events.text: After days of tense, private discussion, members of the [family] family emerge with a decree. They wish for us to wage a righteous war on [rival]. “The learned [character] has apparently done little research into the legal system of [rival], as they continue to support the outdated practice of [law]. The time has come to correct his error and make this vital amendment to their system!”

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Unlawful

Your grievances do not justify bloodshed.

events.text: After days of tense, private discussion, members of the [family] family emerge with a decree. They wish for us to wage a righteous war on [rival]. “[character] is known as a great tactician, but continuing to allow the practice of [law] in [rival] is surely a tactical blunder which will lead his people to defeat and ruin. Especially when we declare war over it.”

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Unlawful

options.text: We will fight because the cause is just.
Your grievances do not justify bloodshed.

events.text: After days of tense, private discussion, members of the [family] family emerge with a decree. They wish for us to wage a righteous war on [rival]. “[character], the zealot, defies gods and men by allowing [rival] to follow the ridiculous practice of [law]. It is clear that the only solution is to convert them by force!”

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: War Groom

options.text: For the good of [rival].
My son will never marry [rival].

events.text: Between the rumors at court and the [rival] troops near our borders, relations with [rival] seem at their worst. You know from past dealings with [character], however, that a path remains open for peace. The [rival] [title] has been looking for a match for his son. You need only give the word to send [character] on his way.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: War and Treachery

options.text: Damn [character] and [character] both. Let them try.
Buy off the [rival] for now. There are more pressing heads to affix to pikes.
And I suppose the threat of war will conveniently recede if [character] takes the throne. So be it. I will not let [rival] burn because I underestimated [character].

events.text: [character] demands tribute, lest [rival] armies wreak havoc through the countryside. And that is not even your most troubling conversation since breakfast. [character] has politely informed your other ministers that unless [rival] forces are put under his command in 'these tumultuous times', he will be mustering his own forces to bring about a 'united government'.

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: War of Schemes

options.text: Send out your trusted agents to plant rumors of another nation preparing to attack them.
We will defeat them on the battlefield and advance to take control of their cities.

events.text: [rival] is preparing for war against us. As soon as the news is confirmed by your agents, plans to distract and confuse the [rival] jump into your scheming mind. Perhaps there is even a way to disrupt and delay their plans?

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: War on the Horizon

options.text: Offer to pay Tribute in the form of knowledge if they agree to stop the war.
Initiate research to pursue a new technological advantage and prepare for battle.

events.text: Emissaries arrive from [rival], accompanied by an intimidating procession of armed guards. Their leader solemnly reads out a formal message from [character], announcing their intent to declare war.

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Wealth or War?

options.text: Pay Tribute in order to keep the peace.
Sometimes, war is the only option.
This is the perfect chance to test and improve new bow designs.

events.text: Emissaries arrive from [rival]. "We have been upset with your people for some time. Unless you are prepared to pay us tribute, those among our court agitating for war may soon get their way."

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Wealth or War?

options.text: Pay Tribute in order to keep the peace.
Sometimes, war is the only option.
We have quietly been testing designs for bows suitable for use from horseback.

events.text: Emissaries arrive from [rival]. "There are those among our court with multiple grievances against your people. Only Tribute could pacify them now."

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Wrath of the Gods

options.text: Order the generals to recruit more men.
Levy a tax to support the coming conflict.
I will ease their concerns with my knowledge of [religion].

events.text: A host of imposing [religion] priests from [rival] descend on the court, startling the guards and servants. They declare that [rival] has angered the adherents of [religion] one too many times, and a judgment is coming. [rival] is a [religion] nation. We should prepare for war.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: [rival] Delenda Est

options.text: Allow him to distract the council with fruitless debates.
Publicly denounce this hothead.
We'll do it, we'll do anything, just please shut him up.

events.text: The Courtier [character] has been making waves, ending all his speeches with a call to eradicate the dangerous rival nation of [rival].

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: [rival] Due

options.text: Defy [rival].

events.text: They say the wealth of the world flows into [city], and it certainly seems as though [character] has been tasked with sending [rival] share.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: [rival] Hegemony

options.text: [character] shall be cordially welcomed in [city].
Any [rival] forces crossing the border shall be cordially welcomed in hell.

events.text: [character], high emissary of [rival], wears an aloof expression and enough finery to purchase a small kingdom. He bears a simple message - [rival] is done waiting, they will bring [rival] into the fold, or they will march on [city]. Should [rival] choose peace, [character] would be installed in a permanent post of oversight, acting as the hand of [character] in [rival].

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: [rival] Looms

options.text: The waiting must end. We will see this through, no matter the cost.
Better to have a headache than a head on a pike.

events.text: Every day, you wait with bated breath for the word that the might of [rival] is bearing down on [city]. What game [character] is playing at you cannot discern, but each day of waiting for the hammer to drop frays your composure yet more.
